subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: What recurring types of problems show up in these incident tickets?

judge.implied_focus: The type/category of problem underlying each incident ticket (recurring problem taxonomy)

per_column.name: problem_type
per_column.rationale: Directly infers and labels the recurring problem category from ticket text, realising the focus of 'types of problems' with a rich, data-inferable taxonomy.

per_column.name: is_connectivity_issue
per_column.rationale: A meaningful roll-up/grouping facet of problem_type, grouping the dominant connectivity-related categories into a higher-level cut analysts can pivot on.

per_column.name: resolution_days
per_column.rationale: Entirely NULL across all 500 rows, so it contributes no signal; conceptually it also pertains to resolution effort/duration, not to inferring the type of problem.

judge.rationale: Two of three columns centre coherently on one inferable focus -- the recurring problem-type taxonomy -- with problem_type providing a granular inferred category and is_connectivity_issue providing a sensible higher-level grouping facet. This is clearly not a scattered grab-bag, and the focus is highly actionable (an analyst can rank, cluster, and prioritise recurring problem classes). Structure quality is dragged down because the set is thin: is_connectivity_issue is largely a derivative restatement of problem_type rather than an orthogonal facet, and resolution_days is completely NULL and off-focus (it addresses resolution time, not problem type), adding no analytical value. A stronger structure would have added orthogonal facets of the problem taxonomy (e.g., affected system/service, root-cause class, severity pattern) rather than a duplicate boolean and an empty column.
